newsitem.title: USA: American Enterprises halts offer for Yale.
newsitem.headline: American Enterprises halts offer for Yale.

text.p: American Enterprises Llc Tuesday terminated its cash tender offer for all of Yale International Inc.'s outstanding common shares after the maker of industrial products accepted a higher bid by Columbus McKinnon Corp.
Richmond, Va.-based American had offered to buy the common of Yale for $16.50, and all outstanding warrants at the spread between $16.50 and the exercise price of the warrants.
Any shares or warrants tendered pursuant to the offer will be returned promptly, the closely held company said.
On Aug. 26 Yale announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by Buffalo, N.Y.-based Columbus McKinnon for $24 per share, or about $260 million in cash.
The combined company would have annual revenues approaching $500 million, with about 3,400 employees.
Yale's stock fell 12.5 cents to $23.25 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.

Yale manufactures and distributes material handling and industrial component products, including chain and wire rope hoists and scissor lifts. It operates under the name Yale International, although its legal identity will remain Spreckels Industries Inc. until shareholder approval is received for the name change at the next annual shareholders meeting.
